title: Safety Zone; Huron River, Huron, OH
summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters of the Huron River within a 150-yard radius of 41[deg]23'34.6" N, 82[deg]33'07.7" W in Huron, OH. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by an over water fireworks show. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Detroit, or their designated representative.

Federal Reserve Bank Services
summary: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) has approved the private-sector adjustment factor (PSAF) for 2027 of $35.3 million and the 2027 fee schedules for Federal Reserve priced services and electronic access. These actions were taken in accordance with the Monetary Control Act of 1980 (MCA), which requires that, over the long run, fees for Federal Reserve priced services be established based on all direct and indirect costs, including the PSAF. Copies of all fee schedules are available from the Federal Reserve Financial Services (FRFS) website at www.FRBservices.org.

title: Accuracy of Advertising and Notice of Insured Status
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing this final rule to streamline its regulations governing advertising and the notice of insured status. This final rule eliminates provisions concerning the official advertising statement. This action is undertaken to reduce regulatory complexity, and the intended effect is to reduce the administrative burden and costs for federally insured credit unions (FICUs) and provide them with greater flexibility in their advertising activities. The final rule does not amend requirements related to displaying the official sign.

title: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information

Nondiscrimination Requirements
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is publishing this final rule to remove a redundant and outdated regulation regarding nondiscrimination in lending. The regulation was intended to summarize the Fair Housing Act (FHA) prohibitions on discrimination related to real estate related loans, appraisals, and advertising. The Board's last substantive amendment to the regulation was finalized in 2001. Thus, the regulation does not reflect all case law or regulatory developments under the FHA, a statute that primarily falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and continues to apply to federal credit unions (FCUs) regardless of this regulation. For these reasons, the Board is removing the regulation in its entirety.

title: Registration of Mortgage Loan Originators
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule to make technical corrections to provisions of the NCUA's regulations. The technical amendments in this final rule improve clarity by removing obsolete references to the registration of mortgage loan originators.

title: Restoring Flexibility To Support Head Start Program Access
summary: In this final rule, the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) removes requirements from the Head Start Program Performance Standards (Performance Standards) to restore local flexibility to Head Start programs and improve access to quality services. Specifically, this final rule removes requirements related to wages and benefits that the Administration believes are not in line with the plain language of the Head Start Act and are costly and overly prescriptive for Head Start programs and staff. ACF estimates these changes will result in over $2 billion in future cost savings for Head Start programs. The rescissions in this final rule impact the costliest parts of the final rule published by the Office of Head Start (OHS) in 2024, Supporting the Head Start Workforce and Consistent Quality Programming.

title: 1,3,4,6,7,8-Hexahydro-4,6,6,7,8,8-hexamethylcyclopenta[γ]-2-benzopyran (HHCB); Risk Evaluation Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Notice of Data Availability and Request for Comment
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is announcing the availability of data and supporting materials related to the draft risk evaluation under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for 1,3,4,6,7,8-Hexahydro-4,6,6,7,8,8-hexamethylcyclopenta[[gamma]]-2- benzopyran (HHCB) (CASRN 1222-05-5). These materials are intended to inform the public and interested parties about the information considered by the Agency in the draft risk evaluation. During the public comment period for the draft risk evaluation of HHCB (April 14, 2026, to June 15, 2026), EPA became aware of an inadvertent administrative issue in its Health and Environmental Research Online (HERO) system that made 24 industry-submitted studies considered in Draft Risk Evaluation for 1,3,4,6,7,8-Hexahydro-4,6,6,7,8,8- hexamethylcyclopenta[[gamma]]-2-benzopyran (HHCB) unavailable to the public. On October 14, 2026, this issue was resolved and the studies were made available to the public in HERO. The Agency invites interested persons to review the newly available materials in the context of the draft risk evaluation and submit comments within a 30- day comment period.
